gallery.title: File:Battle of Dunbar medal.jpg
gallery.credit: Scanned from A J Patrick, The Making Of A Nation 1603-1789, London 1967
gallery.description: Dunbar victory medal showing Cromwell's bust and the Army's battle cry on the day, "The Lord Of Hosts". An official medallist, Mr. Symonds, was depatched to Edinburgh from London to create the Lord General's likeness. Parliament had the medal struck for the combatants, in gold for officers and silver for men. It is believed to be the first medal to be granted to all the ranks of an army and was worn by a cord or chain around the neck.
categories: Military awards and decorations of the United Kingdom

gallery.title: File:Battle of Dunbar, battlefield map, 0430.jpg
gallery.credit: Own work, based on Reese, Peter (2006). Cromwell's Masterstroke: The Battle of Dunbar 1650. Barnsley: Pen and Sword. ISBN 978-1-84415-179-0, p. 82; Reid, Stuart (2008) [2004]. Dunbar 1650: Cromwell's Most Famous Victory. Oxford: Osprey Publishing. ISBN 978-1-84176-774-1, pp. 64–68.
gallery.description:
The Battle of Dunbar took place during the War of the Three Kingdoms, in what is commonly referred to as the "Third English Civil War".
This map depicts the general layout of the two armies just prior to the battle, at 0430.

The Scottish army is labelled in blue, while the English army is in red.
